SMTO-CFG-0043 — SMTO's model request time limit must be above zero

GUID: 4d171e28-970c-422b-8bff-7f756f2c28f5
Slug: config-llm-timeout-seconds-must-be-greater-than
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • A startup setting gives the AI model a time limit for answering each request, but it is set to zero or less, so SMTO stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the settings file (usually config.yaml) in a plain text editor and find timeout_seconds under the llm section. That line sets how long SMTO waits for each model answer.
  2. Change it to a number of seconds from 1 to 1800, or delete the line to use the standard 1800 seconds (30 minutes). Then start SMTO again. SMTO only accepts time limits in that range; zero or less would end every request at once.
  3. Once SMTO is running, fine-tune the time limit in Settings › Setup › Model routing under Limits and recovery, using Request timeout. New work uses the time limit saved there, so you can adjust it without editing the file again.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details (or copy the message from the window where SMTO was started) and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change other timeouts or limits to work around this; only the request time limit is wrong.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Configuration validation failed because the model request timeout (llm.timeout_seconds in the bootstrap YAML, or Settings.llm_timeout_seconds) is zero or negative.

What this means

  • Configured model request timeout_seconds is zero or negative at application settings validation. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Configured model request timeout_seconds is zero or negative at application settings validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish startup positivity validation from the stricter owning client range and generation-progress timeouts.

How to fix it

  • Set llm.timeout_seconds in the bootstrap YAML to a value from 1 to 1800, or omit it for the 1800-second default. The pydantic field constraint (ge=1, le=1800) on LLMConfig.timeout_seconds and Settings.llm_timeout_seconds normally rejects 0 or negative values before this validator runs, so the same mistake may surface as a field-validation error instead. Per-connection request timeouts for new work are configured in Model routing.
  • Choose a positive request timeout within the supported model-client range.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended request timeout passes both startup and model-client validation.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
